summary: Karma Phuntsho works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Oxford under Michael Aris, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Richard Gombrich, later holding posts at CNRS, the University of Cambridge, and Clare Hall, Cambridge.

Karma Sonam Palmo specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed her PhD at the University of Tasmania under Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

Karma Thinley Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He served as abbot of the Young Lamas Home School around 1962–1968 and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling around 1973, and taught Shenpen Hookham and Sam van Schaik.

Karma Ura works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Magdalen College, and the University of Edinburgh, and served as Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH from 1999 to 2008.

Karsé Kongtrul studied under Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, the 13th Dalai Lama, and Khakyab Dorje. His students included Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Khenpo Gangshar.

Karuna Kusalasaya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University and as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Karunesh Shukla works in Indology and Buddhist studies. In 1991, he was Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit and Prakrit Languages at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and founded the Nagarjuna Buddhist Foundation.

Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her education and Habilitation at the University of Bonn and was appointed a full professor at the University of Bern in 1999.

Kashi Prasad Jayaswal worked in Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Allahabad, Jesus College, Oxford, and Lincoln's Inn, later serving as Tagore Professor of Law at the University of Calcutta and president of the Numismatic Society of India.

Kashinath Narayan Dikshit worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held a post at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute and served as Director General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India from 1937 to 1944.

Indologist Kashinath Trimbak Telang studied at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai under Narayan Mahadev Parmanand. He served as Senior Dakshina Fellow at Elphinstone, vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai, and President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar worked in Indology and linguistics. He taught Masaaki Hattori and held posts as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat Arts & Science College and Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Kate Crosby works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She has held posts at Cardiff University, the Buddhist Institute, and SOAS University of London, where she held the Seiyu Kiriyama post in Buddhist Studies.
Kate Wharton specializes in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London by 2008 and was affiliated with Birkbeck, University of London in 2010.
Katharina Sabernig works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD from the University of Vienna by 2017 and has held a post at the Medical University of Vienna.
Katherine Anne Narraway specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She completed her Master of Arts degree at McGill University, where she studied under supervisor G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Katherine Anne Paul works in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Indology. She completed her doctoral studies under Gudrun Bühnemann and was also taught by Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

Katherine Janiec Jones works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied at Davidson College and completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Paul J. Griffiths, having also studied under William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.

Katherine K. Young specializes in Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Chicago and McGill University, and served as a professor at McGill University from around 1978 to 2014.
Katherine Verdery studied at Reed College from 1966 to 1970 and completed her studies at Stanford University between 1970 and 1977. She held a post at the City University of New York around 2005.
